counterfactual_missing_items: A documented recovery of ejection fraction after control of the tachycardias
Thyroid function tests to exclude amiodarone-induced thyrotoxicosis
Temporal evidence that the dual tachycardia preceded the decline in EF
decisive_items: regular atrial tachycardia at cycle length 320ms
response.rationale: R2 is the strongest causal label: it connects the decline in ejection fraction from baseline with the EP-confirmed dual tachycardia, identifying a potentially reversible arrhythmia-driven cardiomyopathy. C1 and R4 capture the heart failure syndrome well, but they stop at the phenotype and do not account for the dual tachycardia or the decrease from baseline. R6 is generic; R5 identifies only one arrhythmia; R3 and R1 lack raw confirmatory findings.

rejected.why: Generic cardiomyopathy; ignores the acute heart failure syndrome and the dual-tachycardia mechanism.
Supported as a heart failure syndrome but superseded by C1's reduced-ejection-fraction subtype and less causal than R2.
Only prior amiodarone use; no raw thyroid laboratory or clinical evidence of thyrotoxicosis.
Atrial tachycardia is part of the dual tachycardia but does not explain the cardiomyopathy or heart failure.
Ejection fraction of 10% is nonspecific; no infiltrative or amyloidosis features are present in the raw vignette.
